sources.title: File:President Reagan's Remarks at Dedication of GM Orion Plant on July 5, 1984.webm

questions.question: What does the speaker recommend doing immediately before a presentation to manage anxiety?
key_answer_facts: Find quiet time, meditate or breathe deeply, and ground yourself.

questions.question: About how many words per minute does the speaker consider optimal?
key_answer_facts: About 150 words per minute, slower for complex information.

questions.question: How does the speaker say presenters build confidence?
key_answer_facts: Practice repeatedly and know the material well.

questions.question: What structure does the speaker recommend for clarity?
key_answer_facts: A clear beginning, middle, and end, with short sentences and repeated key phrases.

questions.question: Why does the speaker recommend combining stories with facts?
key_answer_facts: Stories speak to the heart and make the message more memorable.

questions.question: What is Guy Kawasaki's 10-20-30 rule?
key_answer_facts: Use ten slides, speak for no more than twenty minutes, and use at least thirty-point type.

questions.question: Why can reading dense slide text create a disconnect with the audience?
key_answer_facts: The audience reads ahead faster than the presenter speaks.

questions.question: How does the iceberg analogy apply to presentation data?
key_answer_facts: Slides should show only the small critical part of the research and data available.

questions.question: What does social math do with large statistics?
key_answer_facts: It relates large numbers to familiar things so they are easier to grasp.

questions.question: Which chart types does the speaker associate with trends and parts of a whole?
key_answer_facts: Bar or line charts emphasize trends; pie charts show how numbers correspond to a whole.

questions.question: What advice does the speaker give about using notes?
key_answer_facts: Notes are acceptable; highlighted keywords can prompt the intended points.

questions.question: Which teleprompter brand does the speaker recommend?
What fee should a professional speaker charge?
Which font family is mandatory for all slides?
questions.reason: No mandatory font family is named.

questions.question: How many rehearsals guarantee a successful talk?
questions.reason: No guaranteed rehearsal count is given.

questions.question: How does the lecture distinguish a constant from a variable?
key_answer_facts: A constant is a non-varying value; a variable is a named place in memory whose value can change.

questions.question: What happens to x after assigning 12.2 and later assigning 100?
key_answer_facts: The later assignment replaces 12.2, leaving x equal to 100.

questions.question: What characters may begin a Python variable name?
key_answer_facts: A letter or underscore may begin a variable name, but a number may not.

questions.question: Why are similarly spelled variable names with different capitalization distinct?
key_answer_facts: Python variable names are case sensitive.

questions.question: Why can't reserved words be used as variable names?
key_answer_facts: They have special meanings in Python's core vocabulary.

questions.question: Which side of an assignment statement is calculated first?
key_answer_facts: The right-hand expression is fully calculated before its value is stored on the left.

questions.question: Which symbols does Python use for multiplication, exponentiation, and remainder?
key_answer_facts: Asterisk for multiplication, double asterisk for powers, and percent for remainder.

questions.question: What remainder does the lecture get when dividing 23 by 5?
key_answer_facts: The remainder is 3.

questions.question: What is the stated order of arithmetic operations?
key_answer_facts: Parentheses, exponentiation, multiplication/division/remainder, then addition/subtraction, with ties left to right.

questions.question: Why does the instructor recommend extra parentheses even when they are redundant?
key_answer_facts: They make the intended calculation easier for readers to understand.

questions.question: How does Python 2 integer division differ from floating-point division in the examples?
key_answer_facts: Integer division truncates, while a decimal operand produces a floating-point result.

questions.question: Which Python web framework does the instructor recommend?
How does Python manage garbage collection?
What IDE theme does the instructor use?
Which database driver should beginners install?
What misconception about Wikipedia did the speaker have as an undergraduate?
key_answer_facts: That it was an unverified and unreliable information source.

questions.question: What can readers learn from an article's Talk and View history tabs?
key_answer_facts: Talk shows peer review and editor discussion; View history shows every change and past version.

questions.question: How quickly was the false Babar popularity claim corrected?
key_answer_facts: A Wikipedia editor corrected it in less than two minutes.

questions.question: What does Wikipedia demonstrate about how knowledge is produced?
key_answer_facts: Knowledge production is dynamic and iterative, includes mistakes, and builds on prior work.

questions.question: Why does the speaker connect teaching with contributing to Wikipedia?
key_answer_facts: Teaching something is an effective way to learn it, and editing lets students teach a public audience.

questions.question: What did behavioral ecology students contribute to Wikipedia?
key_answer_facts: They added an animal-behavior perspective, totaling 369,000 words across more than 260 articles.

questions.question: How did the Susan Picard assignment put learning in context?
key_answer_facts: The student integrated history, politics, medicine, and race to build the biography.

questions.question: Why can a Wikipedia assignment motivate students more than a conventional paper?
key_answer_facts: It has a large real audience instead of only one grader.

questions.question: How do Wikipedia editing standards affect student work?
key_answer_facts: Editors can reject weak contributions, motivating careful writing and source evaluation.

questions.question: What help does the Wiki Education Foundation offer instructors?
key_answer_facts: Orientation materials plus help designing timelines, syllabi, assignments, and an interactive course dashboard.

questions.question: How many courses and students had the program reached since 2010?
key_answer_facts: About 1,700 courses and 35,000 students.

questions.question: Does the speaker require students to pay an editing fee?
Which plagiarism detector is integrated with Wikipedia?
What minimum GPA is required to edit an article?
Which university banned the assignment?
When are meeting slides, webcasts, and minutes expected to be posted?
key_answer_facts: Slides within about two weeks, webcasts about four weeks, and minutes about ninety days later.

questions.question: Which three voting members were recognized at their final meeting?
key_answer_facts: Wendy Keitel, Mark Sawyer, and Sarah Rosenbaum.

questions.question: What did Dr. Keitel suggest the zoo study before developing an elephant herpes vaccine?
key_answer_facts: Understand the loss of passive immunity and the age when elephants begin dying.

questions.question: What program did Sarah Rosenbaum design while working for President Clinton?
key_answer_facts: The Vaccines for Children program.

questions.question: What musical activity did Mark Sawyer describe?
key_answer_facts: He plays cello in a community orchestra and chamber groups.

questions.question: Why was Dr. Li Li spending about six months in Atlanta?
key_answer_facts: To learn how the U.S. immunization program and ACIP make evidence-based recommendations.

questions.question: What information must public commenters provide?
key_answer_facts: Their name, organization if appropriate, and conflicts of interest.

questions.question: What did Section 4106 offer states that covered recommended adult preventive services without cost sharing?
key_answer_facts: An additional one percent of federal funds for those services.

questions.question: What electronic-record collaboration did the VA describe?
key_answer_facts: A joint immunization module with DOD and work on access to state immunization registries.

questions.question: What pediatric age range was approved for the Japanese encephalitis vaccine?
key_answer_facts: Two months through seventeen years.

questions.question: Why was NIH exploring multiple flu-vaccine manufacturing techniques?
key_answer_facts: To reduce reliance on egg-based technology for future flu epidemics.

questions.question: What hotel discount was offered to attendees?
Which COVID-19 vaccine did the committee recommend?
questions.reason: The 2013 opening does not discuss a COVID-19 vaccine.

questions.question: What was the meeting's catering budget?
Which smartphone app counted committee votes?
What did Reagan say about the prototype car he drove?
key_answer_facts: It literally drove itself.

questions.question: How much had the auto industry spent since 1979, and how much was GM's U.S. spending?
key_answer_facts: More than $50 billion industry-wide, with over $23 billion spent by GM in America.

questions.question: Why did GM choose the Orion site over cheaper alternatives?
key_answer_facts: To put laid-off GM employees back to work.

questions.question: What did Reagan say management and labor cooperation could accomplish?
key_answer_facts: It could help the industry improve quality, productivity, costs, and compete worldwide.

questions.question: What was the Saturn project's purpose in the speech?
key_answer_facts: To put advanced technology to work so America could lead in new products and jobs.

questions.question: What policy changes did Reagan credit with aiding recovery?
key_answer_facts: Slower federal spending growth, across-the-board tax cuts, indexed tax rates, and reduced regulation.

questions.question: What first-quarter growth and inflation figures did Reagan cite?
key_answer_facts: 9.7 percent economic growth and 3.6 percent inflation.

questions.question: How many jobs and new businesses did the speech say had recently been created?
key_answer_facts: Over six million jobs in eighteen months and over 600,000 new businesses in the prior year.

questions.question: How did Orion employees support their community?
key_answer_facts: They donated to United Way, supported the Christmas food program, and served community organizations.

questions.question: What sales result did GM announce after the speech?
key_answer_facts: June car and truck sales were the best since 1978 and six-month sales were 25 percent ahead of the prior year.

questions.question: Why did employees call the presentation robot Les Junior?
key_answer_facts: It was always on the go, never tired, said little, and did much.

questions.question: What electric-car battery chemistry did the plant adopt?
How many robots worked on each assembly line?
Which foreign automaker supplied the prototype engine?
What was the plant's annual electricity bill?
What three categories of copyright remedy does the lecture introduce?
key_answer_facts: Equitable, legal, and criminal remedies.

questions.question: What is the most common injunction in a copyright suit?
key_answer_facts: An order directing the defendant to stop the infringing behavior.

questions.question: When may a court issue a preliminary injunction?
key_answer_facts: Before the suit ends when the defendant is likely to lose and continued conduct may seriously injure the plaintiff.

questions.question: What must a plaintiff show to obtain a permanent injunction under the traditional test?
key_answer_facts: Irreparable injury, inadequate monetary damages, a favorable hardship balance, and no disservice to the public interest.

questions.question: How does the preliminary-injunction test additionally address the merits?
key_answer_facts: The plaintiff must be likely to succeed in proving the defendant's conduct illegal.

questions.question: Why did the Rear Window court consider money instead of an injunction?
key_answer_facts: The filmmakers had relied in good faith on the original license.

questions.question: When did the Campbell discussion suggest a parody might continue despite infringement?
key_answer_facts: When the defendant pays an appropriate damages award.

questions.question: How did the 2006 eBay decision change the approach to patent injunctions?
key_answer_facts: It rejected near-automatic injunctions and required the traditional equitable factors.

questions.question: Which situations made Justice Kennedy especially reluctant to grant patent injunctions?
key_answer_facts: Patent trolls, patents covering one component of a complex product, and business-method patents.

questions.question: Which appellate cases applied eBay's multifactor tests to copyright injunctions?
key_answer_facts: Salinger and Perfect 10.

questions.question: Why does denying an injunction while awarding damages resemble compulsory licensing?
key_answer_facts: The owner must accept a court-set fee while the defendant continues otherwise forbidden conduct.

questions.question: What prison sentence applies to every copyright violation?
questions.reason: No universal criminal sentence is stated in this segment.

questions.question: Which music platform pays the highest royalty?
questions.reason: No music platform comparison is discussed.

questions.question: What filing fee did the eBay plaintiff pay?
Which country abolished copyright injunctions?
questions.reason: No country is said to abolish them.
